intro: A value update compares a prediction with a target built from the next state. Terminal transitions and rollout cutoffs require different targets.
task: Build one-step value targets and signed temporal-difference errors for a batch of independent transitions.
requirements: The four vector inputs have the same length. terminated contains numeric zero or one, and discount is a scalar in [0,1]. current_values and next_values are supplied value estimates.
Transitions are independent batch rows; never propagate rewards between rows. The error sign is target minus current prediction, and this operation does not update model parameters.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Build the target without the current value
hints.body: The current estimate enters the residual, not the target.

hints.title: Use the terminal mask per row
hints.body: A terminal transition still contributes its observed reward.

explanation: A positive error means the target exceeds the current prediction. This sign matters when a learner later applies a gradient update.
Bootstrapping substitutes a prediction for the unobserved future. If the state truly terminates, there is no future value term to retain.
